title: From Association to Decision Value: Testing Paired Instruction Dependence for VLA Corpus Selection
abstract: arXiv:2610.29646v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Choosing among robot demonstration corpora is a ranking problem: an upstream diagnostic must preserve which candidates produce better downstream policies, not merely correlate with average performance. We study paired instruction dependence, the rate at which a demonstrator changes its first decision when only the goal changes. Across 136 independently seeded quadruped-navigation corpora, predictions developed on 56 corpora are evaluated prospectively on 80 held-out corpora. The audit is reliable and associated with downstream paired correctness, and lowers mean absolute prediction error when added to a correctness-aware baseline, but the primary proper-log-score increment is +0.059 nats (95% corpus-bootstrap CI [-0.027, 0.133]) and the prespecified top-20% comparison does not establish an incremental selection gain. tldr: 该论文提出“配对指令依赖性”作为VLA训练语料库选择的诊断指标，通过136个四足导航语料库的前瞻性评估发现该指标虽然可靠且能降低预测误差，但其增量选择收益尚未在统计上得到确立，并揭示了预测性能与排序价值之间存在结构性不匹配。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes "paired instruction dependence" as a diagnostic metric for VLA training corpus selection, showing through prospective evaluation on 136 quadruped-navigation corpora that while the metric is reliable and reduces prediction error, its incremental selection gain is not statistically established, revealing a structural mismatch between predictive performance and ranking value.
